standard_prerequisites.name: Universal property of n-truncation
standard_prerequisites.statement: For an n-type C, composition with |.|_n is an equivalence from trunc n A -> C to A -> C.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is applied at source lines 619 and 620 to replace trunc n A -> (B -> C) by A -> (B -> C) and trunc n B -> C by B -> C.

standard_prerequisites.name: Function types into an n-type are n-types
standard_prerequisites.statement: If C is an n-type then B -> C is an n-type.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is invoked at source line 623 so that the universal property applies to trunc n A -> (trunc n B -> C).

standard_prerequisites.name: Currying
standard_prerequisites.statement: (A x B -> C) is equivalent to (A -> (B -> C)).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the identification used between the first and last lines of the displayed chain.

core_obligations: Show that trunc n A x trunc n B has the same universal property as trunc n (A x B) (source line 614).
Let C be an n-type and compare mapping spaces, rewriting (trunc n A x trunc n B -> C) as (trunc n A -> (trunc n B -> C)) by currying (source lines 615-618).
Apply the universal property of trunc n B, then that of trunc n A, using that B -> C is an n-type because C is (source lines 619-623).
Identify (A x B -> C) with the mapping space out of trunc n (A x B) and verify that the resulting equivalence is given by composing with |.|_n x |.|_n (source line 624).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the claim to an equality of universal properties and curry the mapping space.
Apply the universal properties of the two truncations and the closure of n-types under function types.
Identify the resulting equivalence with composition by the product of the two unit maps.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.3.8 at source lines 610-612: for any A and B the induced map trunc n (A x B) -> trunc n A x trunc n B is an equivalence. The proof (source lines 613-625) is a comparison of universal properties rather than a construction of an inverse: it is carried out by currying the mapping space into an n-type C (source lines 617-618) and then applying the universal property of truncation twice, for which one must know that B -> C is itself an n-type (source line 623). The last line records that the equivalence obtained this way is the one induced by |.|_n x |.|_n, which is a coherence statement that does not follow from the chain itself. The statement mentions none of this.
